B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Public dollar amounts and plan prices were not found; the vendor directs prospective customers to sales/demo and fees are set in the customer’s Order Form.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: The vendor documents OAuth 2.1 with PKCE and manual API-key authentication. OAuth creates an MCP OAuth PAT linked to the authorizing user; queries inherit that user’s Omni permissions. Organization Admins must enable MCP, and PATs must be enabled for OAuth. The prepared evidence says endpoint OAuth metadata was not fetched because the supplied endpoint is not a concrete public URL; no scopes_supported, token lifetime, registration, or revocation metadata is available.

C_capabilities.authorization_mechanism: OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, or API key. OAuth creates a per-user MCP OAuth PAT. The docs provide an authorization callback URL https://callbacks.omniapp.co/callback/mcp. The API-key endpoint is https://<YOUR_OMNI_INSTANCE>/mcp/https. OAuth metadata and scopes_supported: NOT FETCHED for this instance-specific URL.
C_capabilities.authorization_server: Omni organization instance; OAuth callback/redirect URL documented as https://callbacks.omniapp.co/callback/mcp. Exact authorization-server metadata URL is not available from supplied endpoint.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Read tools and write-capable tools are mixed in the official list. No MCP tool annotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint) were found in docs. 2. Some safeguards exist in product flows: app edits can be drafted then published; deleting a skill through askOmni is described as asking a follow-up if intent is unclear. No general enforced confirmation parameter is documented. 3. OAuth/API keys inherit user/key permissions; OAuth uses OAuth 2.1 with PKCE. Admins enable MCP and feature/tool settings. Token lifetime, scopes, and redirect approval are not documented. 4. No read-only mode is documented. X-MCP-Query-All-Views broadens queryable model views; model/topic headers can scope queries. No sandbox endpoint is documented. 5. Results are scoped to user permissions, model/topic; Omni semantic model governs data access. Exact PII masking is not described. 6. runQuery defaults to 500 rows and caps at 10,000. Dashboard download output caps are 10 MB PNG and 30 MB PDF; one download per user/dashboard at a time. Other rate/cost limits not found. 7. runQuery refuses raw-SQL-triggering keys; documented model header/query model mismatch fails. No general coercion or unknown-argument policy documented. 8. No MCP audit/logging or telemetry details found. 9. submitFeedback records thumbs up/down and optional comment for admin review. 10. listSkills retrieves instructions; askOmni can create, edit, run, and delete skills. Tool recommendations are documented but enforcement beyond stated tool behavior is unknown. 11. Docs describe multi-step analysis and session memory at a high level; durable cross-session behavioral memory is not established. 12. askOmni delegates multi-step work to Omni’s agentic analysis service; no nested MCP server hierarchy is documented. 13. No universal raw API or arbitrary SQL tool is documented; runQuery accepts JSON query definitions and explicitly refuses raw SQL keys.
behavioural_instructions_to_ai_verbatim: Use with checkStatus to prevent timeout issues that can occur when you wait for long-running agentic jobs to complete in a single request.

Changes made with putApp or patchApp land on the document’s shared main draft and are invisible to other viewers until publishDraft runs. The recommended flow is to read the draft with getAppDraft, falling back to getApp only when no draft exists yet, then write, then publish.
Only send dashboards once. Each time a dashboard is sent, it creates a new Omni app. Apps from earlier sends aren’t updated.
Stopping checkStatus polling does not stop the job — use cancelJob to stop it.
D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: One product endpoint is documented with a categorized tool list. askOmni invokes Omni agentic analysis, but no hierarchy of MCP subservers or dynamically loaded toolsets is documented.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: The official tool reference at https://docs.omni.co/ai/mcp/tools names 26 tools; it gives no stated total. actions.json includes all 26 official names plus one catalogue-only name, searchDocs, from APIs.io (2026-10), which is not confirmed in official docs. APIs.io lists 6 tools; 5 match official names and its searchDocs name is additional. Claude connector directory lists 3 tools, all present in the official list. No official source total or category count was published.

E_aggregated.token_method: No public server code or verbatim tools/list and initialize payload was available. The prose tool reference is not sufficient to compute the specified serialized-context estimate.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: The server's tool reference states app settings cannot be changed with its app tools and directs users to the Omni UI. Omni’s broad REST API includes operations not shown in the MCP tool reference; those REST-only operations are outside this MCP tool list. Sources: https://docs.omni.co/ai/mcp/tools and https://docs.omni.co/api

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The docs recommend using checkStatus for long-running jobs and a read-draft/write/publish flow for app changes. These are documented workflows; the docs do not claim the client must follow them. Quote: “The recommended flow is to read the draft with getAppDraft, falling back to getApp only when no draft exists yet, then write, then publish.”
F_documentation.governance_promises: Omni states MCP queries use the authenticated user’s permissions and data access is scoped by model/topic and semantic-layer controls. The docs also note data returned through MCP is present in the client tool. Quote: “By using the MCP Server, your data will be in the tool where you use the MCP Server.”
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Omni describes semantic-model-aware querying and user-level permissioning, and says app rendering uses the same sandboxing and governed queries as elsewhere in Omni.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: User permission inheritance, model/topic scoping, result caps, raw-SQL refusal, and app sandboxing have documented behavior. No reviewed source provides MCP-specific audit logging, telemetry, retention, or PII-masking guarantees. Recommended client workflows are presented as guidance rather than server-enforced confirmation.

contradictions: APIs.io lists searchDocs, while the official reference names searchOmniDocs. The catalogue name is included as an unverified third-party-only action and may be an alternate or stale tool name.
Claude connector directory lists only pickModel, pickTopic, and getData, while the official tool reference names 26 tools; the Claude listing is therefore a subset of documented official tools.
observations_for_research: Tool visibility and tool call authorization differ for Organization API keys: clients may list all admin-enabled tools even when the selected/impersonated user cannot call them; those calls fail.
The broad askOmni tool can do multi-step analysis and create or alter product artifacts, while separate tools expose narrower query and app operations.
The server has both a per-user OAuth identity model and an Organization API key mode that can optionally identify another user through X-MCP-User-ID for supported tools.
notes: Prepared evidence files links.json, links_check.txt, oauth_metadata.txt, pages/ and code/ were checked. No official code repository or commit was provided. OAuth metadata was explicitly NOT FETCHED because the supplied endpoint is per-instance rather than a public concrete URL; consequently scopes_supported and metadata values are unavailable. The official tools page and subpages in pages/ were reviewed; they provide names/descriptions but not input schemas. The unofficial trustxai/omni-mcp repository was noted but excluded. The docs-site search MCP is separate from this product server. Pricing and MCP-specific fees were not found in reviewed vendor materials.
